philosophy: Preferences, not mandates. Prefer these. Override if clearly better. Propose alternatives for important projects (T2+). Never silently drop a favorite — the ADR must state why it was rejected. All listed tools are free to use (OSS or free tier) for personal and commercial projects without paid subscriptions.

tools.name: Rust
tools.description: Systems language with memory safety, zero-cost abstractions, best compiler for AI-generated code
tools.when_to_use: Top priority for everything possible. Performance-critical code, WASM targets, systems tools, CLIs, servers.
tools.notes: Best compiler feedback loop for AI agents — strong type system catches bugs at compile time

tools.name: Python 3
tools.description: General-purpose language, stdlib-first
tools.when_to_use: Prototyping, internal tools, quick builds, data processing, AI/ML
tools.notes: Fast iteration, huge ecosystem, best for AI/ML integration

tools.name: TypeScript
tools.description: Typed superset of JavaScript
tools.when_to_use: Web frontends, React, React Native, Svelte/SvelteKit, Node.js backends

tools.name: Go
tools.description: Simple, fast compilation, excellent concurrency
tools.when_to_use: When Go has a clear ecosystem advantage or specific tooling is Go-native (e.g. Dgraph, Terraform plugins)

tools.name: Clippy
tools.description: Rust linter with 700+ lints, built into cargo
tools.when_to_use: Always for Rust projects

tools.name: rustfmt
tools.description: Rust code formatter, built into cargo
tools.when_to_use: Always for Rust projects

tools.name: cargo test
tools.description: Rust built-in test runner
tools.when_to_use: Always for Rust projects

tools.name: Ruff
tools.description: Fast Python linter and formatter written in Rust
tools.when_to_use: Always for Python projects. Replaces flake8 + black + isort

tools.name: pytest
tools.description: Python testing framework with fixtures and parametrization
tools.when_to_use: Always for Python projects

tools.name: mypy
tools.description: Static type checker for Python
tools.when_to_use: Medium to large Python projects. Optional for small CLI tools.

tools.name: argparse
tools.description: Standard library command-line argument parser
tools.when_to_use: Python CLI tools with simple subcommand structure

tools.name: FastAPI
tools.description: Modern Python web framework with automatic OpenAPI docs
tools.when_to_use: HTTP APIs, web services, backends

tools.name: Biome
tools.description: Rust-based JS/TS linter and formatter, 25x faster than ESLint+Prettier
tools.when_to_use: Always for TypeScript/JavaScript projects

tools.name: Vitest
tools.description: Testing framework for Vite projects
tools.when_to_use: TypeScript/JavaScript projects using Vite

tools.name: Playwright
tools.description: Cross-browser E2E testing
tools.when_to_use: Web apps needing full integration tests

tools.name: Vite
tools.description: Fast bundler and dev server for web projects
tools.when_to_use: Web projects needing bundling, HMR, or build optimization

tools.name: Tailwind CSS
tools.description: Utility-first CSS framework
tools.when_to_use: All web and mobile projects. Foundation for shadcn/ui, gluestack, shadcn-svelte.

tools.name: shadcn/ui
tools.description: Radix + Tailwind, copy-paste components you own
tools.when_to_use: React web apps

tools.name: gluestack v5
tools.description: shadcn-pattern on NativeWind for React Native
tools.when_to_use: React Native / Expo mobile apps

tools.name: shadcn-svelte
tools.description: bits-ui + Tailwind for Svelte, copy-paste components
tools.when_to_use: Svelte/SvelteKit web apps

tools.name: React
tools.description: Component-based UI library
tools.when_to_use: Interactive web apps with complex state

tools.name: Svelte + SvelteKit
tools.description: Compiler-based UI framework with SSR
tools.when_to_use: Web apps, content sites, when you want less boilerplate than React

tools.name: React Native
tools.description: Cross-platform mobile app framework
tools.when_to_use: iOS + Android apps with shared codebase

tools.name: Expo
tools.description: React Native development platform — build, deploy, OTA updates
tools.when_to_use: React Native apps — simplifies everything

tools.name: Tauri
tools.description: Desktop apps with Rust backend + web frontend
tools.when_to_use: Cross-platform desktop apps (Windows/Mac/Linux)

tools.name: ratatui
tools.description: Rust terminal UI framework
tools.when_to_use: Terminal user interfaces in Rust

tools.name: Drizzle ORM
tools.description: TypeScript SQL ORM — schema IS the type system, no codegen
tools.when_to_use: TypeScript projects needing database access. Single source of truth for schema + types.
tools.notes: Schema definition is the type system — no codegen step, no drift. Best migration tooling (drizzle-kit).

tools.name: Drizzle Kit
tools.description: Schema diff migration generator for Drizzle
tools.when_to_use: Always with Drizzle — generates SQL migrations from schema changes

tools.name: axum
tools.description: Rust web framework with ergonomic async, built on hyper/tokio
tools.when_to_use: Rust HTTP APIs and web services

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.description: Production relational database, ACID, feature-rich
tools.when_to_use: Production backends, multi-writer, SaaS, when you need real SQL power

tools.name: Neon
tools.description: Serverless PostgreSQL with branching, scale-to-zero, autoscaling
tools.when_to_use: Serverless Postgres for web apps, when you want branching for preview environments

tools.name: SQLite
tools.description: Embedded relational database, zero-config, file-based
tools.when_to_use: Local-first apps, mobile, CLI tools, prototyping, small services. Use sqlite-vec for vectors and GraphQLite for graph.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.description: Postgres + auth + realtime + storage, open-source Firebase alternative
tools.when_to_use: When you need Postgres + auth + realtime + storage without building each separately

tools.name: Pocketbase
tools.description: Self-hosted BaaS with embedded SQLite, auth, realtime
tools.when_to_use: Self-hosted alternative to Supabase. Single binary, simpler.

tools.name: MongoDB
tools.description: Document database with flexible schema
tools.when_to_use: When schema is genuinely unknown or rapidly evolving, content management, event logs

tools.name: Qdrant
tools.description: Vector database for AI/RAG, HNSW + quantization, scales to billions
tools.when_to_use: Production vector search at scale, RAG, semantic search beyond what sqlite-vec can handle

tools.name: sqlite-vec
tools.description: SQLite extension for vector search, pure C, runs in WASM/browser/mobile
tools.when_to_use: Embedded/local-first vector search up to ~1M vectors. Brute-force KNN — fine for small sets.

tools.name: SurrealDB
tools.description: Multi-model: document + graph + vector + key-value in one engine. SurrealQL. Rust.
tools.when_to_use: When you need multiple data models in one engine (graph + doc + vector). Runs embedded (like SQLite), in WASM/browser, or as server. BSL 1.1 (converts to Apache 2.0 in 2030).

tools.name: Dgraph
tools.description: Distributed graph DB that auto-generates GraphQL APIs. Apache 2.0. Go.
tools.when_to_use: When you want native GraphQL backend from schema, distributed scale. Fully Apache 2.0 — safest license.

tools.name: Neo4j Community Edition
tools.description: Most mature graph DB. Cypher. Native graph storage. GPLv3.
tools.when_to_use: When you need the most mature graph ecosystem, Cypher expertise, GDS library, or GraphRAG. CE = single instance, no clustering. GPLv3 is SaaS-safe (not AGPL).

tools.name: Memgraph
tools.description: In-memory graph DB, sub-ms multi-hop, Cypher, GraphRAG. C++.
tools.when_to_use: Real-time graph analytics, GraphRAG, when latency matters most. BSL 1.1 (converts to Apache 2.0 in 2030). In-memory — bounded by RAM.

tools.name: FalkorDB
tools.description: Graph DB using GraphBLAS sparse matrix math, Redis-compatible. Rust. SSPL-1.0.
tools.when_to_use: When you already run Redis, need ultra-low-latency graph traversal, Cypher queries. SSPL — fine for SaaS, can't offer as hosted service.

tools.name: GraphQLite
tools.description: SQLite extension for graph DB with Cypher, algorithms built-in. C.
tools.when_to_use: Embedded/local-first graph on top of SQLite. The only client-side graph option. 97.7% openCypher conformance. Built-in PageRank, Louvain, Dijkstra.

tools.name: ArangoDB
tools.description: Multi-model: graph + document + key-value in one engine. AQL query language. C++.
tools.when_to_use: When you want one database for graph + documents + key-value. BSL 1.1.

tools.name: Cloudflare D1
tools.description: Serverless SQLite on Cloudflare's edge network
tools.when_to_use: When backend is on Cloudflare Workers/Pages. SQLite-compatible.

tools.name: Cloudflare Queues
tools.description: Managed message queues on Cloudflare edge
tools.when_to_use: When backend is on Cloudflare Workers and you need async task processing

tools.name: Redis
tools.description: In-memory key-value store, caching, pub/sub, rate limiting
tools.when_to_use: Caching, session storage, rate limiting, pub/sub. Almost every SaaS needs it.

tools.name: RabbitMQ
tools.description: Message broker for async task processing
tools.when_to_use: Reliable async task queues, event-driven architectures, work distribution

tools.name: BullMQ
tools.description: TypeScript job queue on Redis
tools.when_to_use: TypeScript background job processing, when you already have Redis

tools.name: Better Auth
tools.description: MIT-licensed, TypeScript-native auth, self-hosted, unlimited, passkey/SSO/OIDC plugins
tools.when_to_use: Primary auth for TypeScript backends. Run as TS service, validate JWTs in Python/Rust backends.

tools.name: Logto
tools.description: Standalone OIDC server, native TS + Python SDKs, Expo support
tools.when_to_use: When you need a standalone auth server with native Python SDK. Apache 2.0.

tools.name: SuperTokens
tools.description: Auth with native Python/FastAPI SDK. Self-hosted, free.
tools.when_to_use: When backend is Python/FastAPI and you want native SDK auth

tools.name: Stripe
tools.description: Payment processing, subscriptions, billing
tools.when_to_use: SaaS billing, ecommerce, subscription management

tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
tools.description: TypeScript SDK for building AI apps, streaming, tool calling
tools.when_to_use: TypeScript AI applications, streaming responses, tool calling

tools.name: Mastra
tools.description: TypeScript agent framework
tools.when_to_use: Building AI agents in TypeScript

tools.name: rust-genai
tools.description: Rust crate for LLM API calls, multi-provider
tools.when_to_use: Rust projects needing LLM integration

tools.name: pydantic-ai
tools.description: Python AI agent framework with type safety
tools.when_to_use: Python AI agents with type-safe tool calling

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.description: Python graph-based agent orchestration
tools.when_to_use: Complex multi-agent orchestration in Python

tools.name: OpenAI-compatible APIs
tools.description: Any LLM provider with OpenAI-compatible API surface
tools.when_to_use: Top priority for all AI/LLM work. Always prefer OpenAI-compatible providers first for portability.
tools.notes: Always prioritize OpenAI-compatible APIs for portability across providers

tools.name: Temporal
tools.description: Durable execution engine for long-running workflows
tools.when_to_use: Complex multi-step workflows, saga patterns, process orchestration

tools.name: Inngest
tools.description: TypeScript-first durable workflows, simpler than Temporal
tools.when_to_use: TypeScript projects needing durable workflows, background jobs, retries

tools.name: pi coding agent SDK
tools.description: SDK for building coding agents
tools.when_to_use: Building AI coding assistants and code-aware agents

tools.description: Go meta-linter aggregating multiple linters

tools.when_to_use: Always for Go projects
